howItWorks.title: How it works
howItWorks.intro: This is what happens after you report, in plain steps.

p: You tell us what happened using a short form and can add screenshots. You get a tracking code. Keep it safe. It is the only way to add evidence or withdraw later, and we cannot show it to you again.
A member of our team calls the number you gave to confirm the report is yours. We do not publish your number.

sections.h: 3. We check it and send it on
p: We review each report in the order received. If it is in scope, we send a case file to the right authority.
Each time an authority replies, we log the date and the type of reply. We do not copy what the authority wrote.

Only a short neutral summary written by our team appears in the public ledger, with the authority, the status and the dates. It never contains names, images, links, phone numbers or anything you wrote.

ul: Sharing or leaking intimate images or video without consent
Sextortion and blackmail involving intimate content
Online sexual harassment
Online sexual exploitation or trafficking (adult victims on this website)

p: Hate speech, defamation disputes, political or expression cases, fraud, and any dispute where the harm is not sexual or non-consensual.
We do not take reports about people under 18. The referral page explains how to complain directly to the right bodies.
You can withdraw a report at any time with your tracking code.

methodology.title: Methodology
methodology.intro: What we publish, what we never publish, and how every figure is counted.

ul: Case ID and dates
A broad category
A short summary written by our team
The authority the case was sent to
The type and date of the latest reply
The status, and the closing reason when a case is closed
Whether a resubmission was requested
When the row was last updated
Names of anyone
Images, video, audio or screenshots
Phone numbers
Profile links or usernames
Anything the reporter wrote
Names of officers. Only the authority is shown

sections.h: How the top figures are counted
ul: Cases sent to authorities: every case we have forwarded to an authority.
Awaiting a reply: forwarded cases that are not closed and have no reply from the authority yet. A logged "no reply" does not count as a reply.
Under investigation: cases where the authority has told us action is under way.
Closed, resolved: cases with a closing event whose outcome is recorded as resolved from the authority's correspondence.
Closed, unresolved: cases closed without a resolved outcome. Each has a reason.
Median time to first reply: the middle value of the days between sending a case and the authority's first acknowledgement.
p: Every figure comes from logged, dated events. [VERIFY: owner to confirm these definitions before launch]

A case shows one status at a time: submitted, acknowledged, under investigation, additional information requested, resubmission requested, no response (after a set number of days), closed and resolved, or closed and unresolved.
Dates and times are shown in Sri Lanka time.

about.title: About and independence
about.intro: Who runs this project and what it is not.

p: SLCCRAOP is an independent civil-society project. It is not part of, endorsed by, or acting for any government body or police force.
The word “Registry” in our name does not mean we are an official registry.
{{ownerPublicName}}

We help people report online sexual abuse and non-consensual sexual content, pass verified cases to the right Sri Lankan authority, and show publicly, without naming anyone, how each authority responds over time.
We are not an emergency service, a court or a law firm. We do not investigate cases and we do not give legal advice.
